text: Background: Night-shift work has been associated with an elevated risk of type 2 diabetes, but the extent to which circadian misalignment impairs glucose tolerance in otherwise healthy workers remains uncertain. Methods: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 412 hospital nurses aged 25 to 55 years without diabetes at baseline, comparing those on rotating night shifts with those working day shifts only. Oral glucose tolerance tests were performed at enrollment and after 24 months, and continuous glucose monitoring was used in a subsample of 96 participants. Results: After adjustment for age, body mass index, physical activity, and diet quality, rotating night-shift work was associated with a significantly greater increase in two-hour post-load glucose and a higher incidence of impaired glucose tolerance. Glycemic variability was most pronounced following consecutive night shifts. Conclusions: Rotating night-shift work independently predicts deterioration in glucose tolerance among healthy nurses, supporting the need for targeted metabolic screening in shift-working populations.

Objective: To evaluate whether structured telehealth follow-up improves functional outcomes and reduces hospital readmissions after ischemic stroke compared with usual outpatient care. Design: Multicenter randomized controlled trial. Participants: A total of 538 adults discharged home after a first ischemic stroke were randomly assigned to a 12-week telehealth program, consisting of weekly video consultations with a stroke nurse, remote blood pressure monitoring, and medication review, or to standard follow-up. Main outcome measures: The primary outcome was the modified Rankin Scale score at 90 days; secondary outcomes included 90-day readmission, blood pressure control, and patient-reported quality of life. Results: Participants in the telehealth group were more likely to achieve functional independence and had fewer all-cause readmissions, while improvements in blood pressure control and medication adherence were also observed. No safety concerns were identified. Conclusion: A low-cost telehealth follow-up program improved early recovery after stroke and may represent a scalable strategy for post-discharge care.

Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity worldwide, yet their contribution to preterm birth in low-resource settings has not been well quantified. In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed records of 18,240 singleton deliveries at three referral hospitals between 2016 and 2021. Hypertensive disorders, including chronic hypertension, gestational hypertension, and preeclampsia, were identified from clinical documentation, and associations with spontaneous and medically indicated preterm birth were estimated using multivariable logistic regression. Hypertensive disorders were present in 9.6 percent of pregnancies and were associated with a more than twofold increase in the odds of preterm birth, driven predominantly by medically indicated deliveries in women with preeclampsia with severe features. The association remained robust after adjustment for maternal age, parity, and antenatal care attendance. These findings highlight the importance of early detection and management of hypertension during pregnancy as a strategy to reduce preterm birth.

Dietary fiber has been proposed as a modifiable factor in colorectal cancer prevention, but evidence regarding its effect on the recurrence of colorectal adenomas is inconsistent. We performed a secondary analysis of a prospective surveillance cohort including 1,327 patients who underwent complete removal of at least one adenoma. Habitual fiber intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire, and recurrence was ascertained by follow-up colonoscopy over a median of 3.8 years. Higher intake of cereal fiber was associated with a reduced risk of advanced adenoma recurrence, whereas fiber from fruit and vegetables showed no significant association. The protective effect appeared stronger among participants with lower red meat consumption. Although residual confounding cannot be excluded, these results suggest that the source of dietary fiber may be relevant to secondary prevention and warrant evaluation in randomized dietary interventions.

Knee osteoarthritis is a major cause of pain and disability in older adults, and exercise therapy is widely recommended as first-line treatment. However, the relative effectiveness of different exercise modalities remains unclear. This systematic review and network meta-analysis synthesized data from 74 randomized trials involving 6,102 participants with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis. Interventions included strengthening, aerobic, aquatic, mind-body, and mixed exercise programs. Strengthening exercise ranked highest for pain reduction, while mixed programs combining strength and aerobic components produced the greatest improvements in physical function. Aquatic exercise yielded moderate benefits, particularly among participants with obesity. The certainty of evidence was rated as moderate for most comparisons, and heterogeneity was largely explained by differences in program duration and supervision. These findings support tailoring exercise prescriptions to individual treatment goals and suggest that supervised programs of at least eight weeks are most likely to deliver meaningful benefit.

Concerns about the effects of screen time on adolescent mental health have intensified in recent years, but most existing studies rely on cross-sectional data and self-reported usage. Using four waves of longitudinal data from a nationally representative sample of 7,830 adolescents aged 12 to 16, we examined the bidirectional relationship between objectively measured smartphone use and depressive symptoms. Random-intercept cross-lagged panel models were used to separate stable between-person differences from within-person change over time. At the between-person level, higher average smartphone use was modestly associated with more depressive symptoms. Within individuals, however, increases in smartphone use did not predict subsequent increases in depressive symptoms; instead, elevated depressive symptoms predicted greater subsequent use. Effects were small in magnitude and did not differ substantially by gender. These results caution against causal interpretations of screen time as a primary driver of adolescent depression.

Health care workers face an elevated risk of occupational exposure to hepatitis B virus, yet vaccination coverage in many settings remains incomplete. This cross-sectional study assessed hepatitis B vaccination status, post-vaccination serological testing, and associated factors among 1,146 health care workers employed at public hospitals in two regions. Data were collected through structured interviews and verified against occupational health records where available. Overall, 61.2 percent of participants reported receiving the full three-dose series, while only 18.4 percent had undergone testing to confirm immunity. Full vaccination was more common among physicians and nurses than among cleaning and laboratory support staff, and was strongly associated with prior infection control training and free provision of the vaccine by the employer. These findings reveal substantial gaps in protection, particularly among lower-paid staff, and underscore the need for mandatory, employer-funded vaccination programs with routine serological follow-up.

Sarcopenia, the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function, is highly prevalent among patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis and is linked to frailty and mortality. We investigated the prevalence and prognostic significance of sarcopenia, defined according to the revised European consensus criteria, in 356 adults undergoing hemodialysis at four dialysis centers. Muscle mass was estimated by bioelectrical impedance analysis, strength by handgrip dynamometry, and physical performance by gait speed. Sarcopenia was identified in 38.5 percent of patients and was more common among older individuals, those with diabetes, and those with lower serum albumin. During a median follow-up of 31 months, sarcopenia was independently associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality and hospitalization. Notably, low muscle strength was a stronger predictor of adverse outcomes than low muscle mass. Routine assessment of muscle strength may therefore offer a practical approach to risk stratification in dialysis care.

Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids have been investigated as an adjunctive treatment for depression, with mixed results. In this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 248 adults with mild to moderate major depressive disorder were randomized to receive either 2 grams per day of eicosapentaenoic acid-predominant fish oil or a matched placebo for 12 weeks in addition to usual care. The primary outcome was change in the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale score. Both groups improved over the study period, and the difference between them did not reach statistical significance in the primary analysis. In a prespecified subgroup analysis, however, participants with elevated baseline inflammatory markers showed a significantly greater response to omega-3 supplementation. Adverse events were mild and comparable between groups. These findings suggest that omega-3 supplementation is unlikely to benefit unselected patients with depression but may be effective in an inflammatory subtype, a hypothesis that merits confirmation in an adequately powered trial.

Inpatient falls remain a persistent threat to patient safety, and nurse staffing has been proposed as an important organizational determinant. We linked shift-level staffing data with incident reports from 52 medical and surgical wards across 11 hospitals over a 36-month period, encompassing more than 1.9 million patient-days. Multilevel negative binomial models were used to estimate associations between registered nurse hours per patient-day, skill mix, and the rate of falls and injurious falls, adjusting for patient acuity and ward characteristics. Each additional registered nurse hour per patient-day was associated with a lower rate of falls, and wards with a higher proportion of registered nurses relative to assistive staff experienced fewer injurious falls. Shifts staffed below planned levels showed a marked increase in risk. These results indicate that adequate registered nurse staffing is a key component of fall prevention and should inform workforce planning decisions in acute care.

Accumulating evidence suggests that access to urban green space may benefit cardiovascular health, yet the underlying pathways remain poorly understood. Drawing on data from 22,415 adults in a population-based cohort residing in 14 cities, we examined associations between residential greenness, measured by the normalized difference vegetation index within a 500-meter buffer, and blood pressure. Greater residential greenness was associated with lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure and a reduced prevalence of hypertension, independent of individual and neighborhood socioeconomic status. Mediation analyses indicated that a substantial proportion of this association was explained by higher levels of physical activity and lower exposure to traffic-related air pollution and noise, while the role of reduced psychological stress was more modest. The associations were strongest among older adults and residents of lower-income neighborhoods. These findings support the integration of green infrastructure into urban planning as a population-level strategy for cardiovascular prevention.

Hip fracture in older adults is associated with high rates of functional decline and mortality, and early mobilization after surgery has been proposed to improve recovery. This quality improvement study evaluated the implementation of a protocol requiring patients to sit out of bed and attempt standing within 24 hours of hip fracture surgery at a regional teaching hospital. Outcomes for 487 patients treated after implementation were compared with those of 455 patients treated in the preceding two years. Following implementation, the proportion of patients mobilized within 24 hours increased from 41 to 83 percent. Early mobilization was associated with a shorter length of stay, a lower incidence of postoperative pneumonia and delirium, and a higher likelihood of discharge directly to home, without an increase in surgical complications. These findings demonstrate that a simple, nurse- and physiotherapist-led protocol can be implemented effectively and may improve outcomes for this vulnerable population.

Accurate prediction of crop yields is essential for food security planning, particularly in regions vulnerable to climate variability. In this study, we developed and evaluated a machine learning framework for predicting maize yields at the district level by integrating satellite-derived vegetation indices, gridded weather data, and soil properties. We compared random forest, gradient boosting, and long short-term memory models trained on 15 years of yield records from 284 districts. The gradient boosting model achieved the best performance, explaining 78 percent of the variance in out-of-sample yields, and its predictions remained reliable up to two months before harvest. Feature importance analysis identified mid-season vegetation indices and cumulative rainfall during the flowering stage as the most influential predictors. Model accuracy declined in years with extreme drought, highlighting the challenge of forecasting under unprecedented conditions. The framework offers a practical, data-driven tool to support early warning systems and agricultural policy.

Microplastic contamination of freshwater ecosystems has become an emerging environmental concern, but data on its accumulation in wild fish remain limited. We examined the gastrointestinal tracts of 640 fish representing nine species collected from 18 river and lake sites spanning urban, agricultural, and protected catchments. Microplastic particles were extracted by alkaline digestion and identified using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. Microplastics were detected in 47 percent of individuals, with fibers being the most common morphology and polyethylene and polyester the most prevalent polymers. Contamination was significantly higher at urban sites located downstream of wastewater treatment plants and among benthic feeding species. Body condition was not associated with microplastic burden in most species. These results indicate that wastewater effluent is a major pathway for microplastic entry into freshwater food webs and suggest that improved filtration at treatment facilities could substantially reduce exposure for aquatic wildlife.

The rapid expansion of remote and hybrid work has raised important questions about its implications for employee wellbeing. Drawing on a two-wave panel survey of 3,214 knowledge workers across 46 organizations, this study examines how work arrangement, job autonomy, and boundary management relate to burnout, work engagement, and life satisfaction. Fully remote employees reported greater autonomy and lower commuting stress but also higher levels of professional isolation and difficulty disconnecting from work. Hybrid arrangements were associated with the most favorable overall outcomes, particularly when employees retained discretion over which days to work on site. Strong boundary management practices buffered the negative effects of remote work on burnout. These findings suggest that the wellbeing effects of remote work depend less on location itself than on how work is organized, and they offer practical guidance for organizations designing flexible work policies.

Research on whether bilingualism confers advantages in executive function has produced conflicting findings, partly owing to methodological differences across studies. In this preregistered study, we compared 312 children aged 7 to 10 enrolled in dual-language immersion programs with 298 children in monolingual programs, matched on socioeconomic background and nonverbal intelligence. Executive function was assessed using a battery of tasks measuring inhibitory control, working memory, and cognitive flexibility, administered at the beginning and end of the school year. Children in dual-language programs did not differ significantly from their peers on inhibitory control or working memory. A small advantage was observed in cognitive flexibility, which was larger among children with greater proficiency in their second language. Taken together, the results do not support a broad bilingual advantage in executive function but suggest that specific, proficiency-dependent benefits may exist. Implications for educational policy and future research are discussed.

Graphene-based materials are attractive candidates for supercapacitor electrodes owing to their high theoretical surface area and electrical conductivity, but restacking of graphene sheets limits their practical performance. Here we report a scalable method for fabricating three-dimensional nitrogen-doped graphene aerogels incorporating vertically aligned carbon nanotube spacers. The resulting electrodes exhibit a hierarchical porous structure that preserves accessible surface area and facilitates rapid ion transport. In aqueous electrolyte, the material delivers a specific capacitance of 312 farads per gram at a current density of 1 ampere per gram and retains 94 percent of its capacitance after 10,000 charge-discharge cycles. A symmetric device assembled from these electrodes achieves an energy density competitive with commercial activated carbon devices while sustaining high power output. Spectroscopic analysis indicates that pyridinic nitrogen sites contribute significantly to pseudocapacitive behavior. This approach offers a promising route toward high-performance, durable energy storage devices.

Urban heat islands intensify the health risks of extreme heat, yet the spatial distribution of heat-related mortality within cities is rarely quantified. We combined high-resolution land surface temperature data with daily mortality records for 1.2 million deaths occurring between 2005 and 2019 across 31 metropolitan areas. Using a case-crossover design, we estimated the excess risk of death associated with heat exposure at the neighborhood level. On extremely hot days, mortality risk increased substantially, and the effect was markedly greater in neighborhoods with a stronger heat island effect, characterized by limited tree cover and high impervious surface area. Older adults and residents of socioeconomically disadvantaged areas experienced the largest excess risk. We estimate that approximately one in five heat-related deaths could be attributed to the additional warming produced by the urban heat island. Targeted greening and cooling interventions in vulnerable neighborhoods could therefore yield substantial public health benefits.

Social media platforms are frequently blamed for rising political polarization, but causal evidence remains scarce. In a field experiment conducted during a national election campaign, we randomly assigned 2,840 adult social media users either to deactivate their accounts for four weeks or to continue using them as usual. Outcomes were measured through surveys administered before and after the intervention period, supplemented by behavioral data on news consumption. Deactivation led to a modest reduction in affective polarization, particularly in hostility toward members of the opposing party, but had no significant effect on issue-based polarization or factual political knowledge. Participants who deactivated also reported small improvements in subjective wellbeing and spent more time on offline social activities. The effects faded within two months after reactivation. These findings suggest that social media contributes to affective polarization but that its influence is narrower and less durable than commonly assumed.

Cover crops are widely promoted as a strategy for sequestering soil organic carbon in agricultural systems, but estimates of their long-term effect vary widely. We conducted a meta-analysis of 128 field studies reporting paired measurements of soil organic carbon under cover-cropped and bare fallow treatments. On average, cover cropping increased soil organic carbon stocks in the upper 30 centimeters by an amount equivalent to roughly 0.3 megagrams of carbon per hectare per year. Gains were larger in systems using legume and grass mixtures, under no-till management, and in soils with initially low carbon content, while effects in deeper soil layers were inconsistent and often undetectable. Sequestration rates declined over time as soils approached a new equilibrium. These results confirm that cover crops can contribute meaningfully to soil carbon storage but indicate that their climate mitigation potential is finite and should be evaluated alongside other agronomic and environmental benefits.

Feedback is among the most powerful influences on student learning, yet its effects on motivation depend heavily on how it is delivered. This mixed-methods study investigated the relationship between the type of written teacher feedback and student motivation in 42 secondary school classrooms. Over one semester, we analyzed 3,600 instances of feedback on student assignments, coding them as evaluative, directive, or elaborative, and surveyed 1,108 students on intrinsic motivation, self-efficacy, and perceived teacher support. Elaborative feedback that explained the reasoning behind suggestions and identified specific next steps was positively associated with both intrinsic motivation and self-efficacy, whereas purely evaluative comments showed no association or a slightly negative one. Follow-up interviews revealed that students valued feedback they perceived as actionable and personalized. The findings highlight the importance of feedback quality over quantity and have implications for teacher professional development.

Earthquake early warning systems aim to detect the initial seismic waves of an earthquake and issue alerts before strong shaking arrives, but their effectiveness depends on rapid and accurate magnitude estimation. We present a deep learning approach that estimates earthquake magnitude and expected ground shaking from the first three seconds of waveform data recorded at a single station. The model, a convolutional neural network trained on more than 400,000 three-component seismograms, was evaluated on an independent test set of earthquakes from a different time period. It estimated magnitude with a mean absolute error of 0.27 units and maintained reliable performance for large events, which have historically been underestimated by conventional methods. Compared with the existing operational algorithm, our approach increased the average warning time for strongly shaken sites by several seconds. These results demonstrate the potential of machine learning to improve the speed and reliability of earthquake early warning.

The growth of ride-hailing services has transformed urban mobility, but their effect on traffic congestion remains contested. Using a difference-in-differences design that exploits the staggered entry of a major ride-hailing platform into 89 metropolitan areas, we estimate the impact of ride-hailing on road congestion and public transit ridership. Congestion was measured using vehicle speed data from GPS traces, and transit ridership was obtained from agency records. We find that ride-hailing entry was followed by a significant increase in congestion, as measured by travel time delays during peak hours, alongside a modest decline in bus ridership. The effects grew over time as ride-hailing adoption increased and were largest in dense urban cores. Heterogeneity analyses suggest that much of the additional traffic stems from deadheading, the distance driven without passengers between trips. These results inform ongoing policy debates about congestion pricing and the regulation of ride-hailing services.

Electric buses are increasingly adopted by transit agencies seeking to reduce emissions, but uncertainty about battery degradation complicates fleet planning and lifecycle cost estimates. We analyzed operational data from 214 battery electric buses operated by six transit agencies over periods of up to seven years, including charging records, ambient temperature, route characteristics, and periodic capacity measurements. Battery capacity declined by an average of 2.1 percent per year, a rate slower than manufacturers' conservative projections. Degradation was accelerated by frequent fast charging, high average state of charge during overnight storage, and operation in regions with extreme temperatures. Buses operating on routes with steep gradients also showed modestly faster capacity loss. Using these results, we developed a predictive model of battery health that can inform charging strategies and replacement schedules. Our findings suggest that adjusting charging practices could extend battery life substantially, improving the economic case for fleet electrification.

Despite strong evidence of its effectiveness, human papillomavirus vaccine uptake remains low in many rural communities. This cluster-randomized trial evaluated a school-based intervention designed to increase HPV vaccination among adolescents aged 11 to 13 in 36 rural schools. Intervention schools received a combined program of parent education sessions, reminder messages, and on-site vaccination clinics, while control schools continued with standard practice. Vaccination records were obtained from state immunization registries 12 months after the start of the intervention. Initiation of the vaccine series was substantially higher in intervention schools than in control schools, and completion of the recommended doses also increased. Effects were consistent across sexes and socioeconomic groups. Parent surveys indicated that the education sessions reduced concerns about vaccine safety, while the on-site clinics addressed barriers related to travel and scheduling. The findings support school-based delivery as a practical strategy for improving HPV vaccine coverage in underserved rural areas.
